spawn.title: How tokio::spawn works
spawn.description: Starts a new asynchronous task that runs alongside the current one.

slides.caption: A spawned task runs on its own; await its JoinHandle to get its result (or the panic it ended with).
The new task is scheduled on the runtime.
The caller keeps going; awaiting the handle gives Ok(3).
The future must be Send + 'static: move the data it needs into it.

spawn-blocking.title: How tokio::task::spawn_blocking works
spawn-blocking.description: Runs blocking code on a separate thread pool, so async tasks keep running.

slides.caption: Blocking inside an async task stalls every other task on that thread. spawn_blocking moves the work away.
The closure runs on a blocking-pool thread.
Awaiting the handle gives its return value.
Use it for CPU-heavy work, sync file I/O, or sync libraries.

yield-now.title: How tokio::task::yield_now works
yield-now.description: Gives other tasks a chance to run before continuing.

slides.caption: Async tasks are only paused at .await points.
Useful inside long loops that rarely await.
The task stops at its next .await; awaiting the handle gives a JoinError.
Dropping a JoinHandle does NOT cancel the task.

join-handle-is-finished.title: How JoinHandle::is_finished works
join-handle-is-finished.description: true once the task has completed.

slides.caption: Await the handle to get the result.

joinset-spawn.title: How JoinSet::spawn works
joinset-spawn.description: Spawns a task into a set, so you can wait for all of them as they finish.

slides.caption: A JoinSet owns its tasks: dropping the set aborts them.
Each spawn adds a task to the set.
len() counts the tasks not yet joined.
Collect the results with join_next() or join_all().

joinset-join-next.title: How JoinSet::join_next works
joinset-join-next.description: Waits for the next task of the set to finish, in finishing order.

slides.caption: Returns None when the set is empty.
Order is by completion, not by spawn.

joinset-join-all.title: How JoinSet::join_all works
joinset-join-all.description: Waits for every task and returns their results in a Vec.

joinset-abort-all.title: How JoinSet::abort_all works
joinset-abort-all.description: Cancels every task in the set.

slides.caption: They stay in the set until joined; join_next then reports cancellation.
Dropping the set also aborts them.

sleep.title: How tokio::time::sleep works
sleep.description: Waits for a duration without blocking the thread.

slides.caption: std::thread::sleep would block every task on this thread. tokio's sleep only pauses the current task.
The task registers a timer and yields.
The runtime wakes it when the time is up.
Remember the .await: without it nothing happens.

timeout.title: How tokio::time::timeout works
timeout.description: Gives a future a time limit: Ok(value) if it finishes in time, Err(Elapsed) if not.

slides.caption: timeout races the future against a timer.
The fast one finishes first: Ok.
The timer fires first: Err(Elapsed), and the slow future is cancelled.
Wrap network calls with it so they cannot hang forever.

interval.title: How tokio::time::interval works
interval.description: A timer that ticks every period; the first tick is immediate.

slides.caption: Missed ticks catch up by default (MissedTickBehavior::Burst).
sleep in a loop would drift; interval keeps the rhythm.

interval-tick.title: How Interval::tick works
interval-tick.description: Waits until the next tick of the interval.

slides.caption: The first call returns at once.
Use it at the top of a loop body.

note.text: result: second tick after ≥ 30 ms: true

slides.caption: Good for deadlines shared by several steps.
tokio::time::Instant works with the runtime's clock.

mpsc-channel.title: How tokio::sync::mpsc::channel works
mpsc-channel.description: A bounded queue between tasks: many senders, one receiver.

slides.caption: When the buffer is full, send().await waits: this is how a slow receiver slows down fast senders (backpressure).
Senders push messages; clone tx for more producers.
The receiver gets them in order.
recv() returns None once every sender is dropped.

mpsc-send.title: How mpsc::Sender::send works
mpsc-send.description: Sends a value, waiting while the channel is full.

slides.caption: Err(SendError(value)) if the receiver is gone; you get the value back.

mpsc-try-send.title: How mpsc::Sender::try_send works
mpsc-try-send.description: Sends only if there is room right now; never waits.

slides.caption: Err(Closed) if the receiver is gone.

mpsc-recv.title: How mpsc::Receiver::recv works
mpsc-recv.description: Waits for the next message; None when all senders are gone and the queue is empty.

slides.caption: recv() is the usual loop condition: while let Some(msg) = rx.recv().await { ... }.
Queue empty and no senders left: None ends the loop.
Keep a sender alive (or clone it) as long as messages may come.

mpsc-try-recv.title: How mpsc::Receiver::try_recv works
mpsc-try-recv.description: Takes a message if one is ready; never waits.

slides.caption: Err(Disconnected) when all senders are gone.

mpsc-recv-many.title: How mpsc::Receiver::recv_many works
mpsc-recv-many.description: Receives up to n waiting messages into a Vec in one call.

slides.caption: Waits only if nothing is available.

unbounded-channel.title: How tokio::sync::mpsc::unbounded_channel works
unbounded-channel.description: A channel without a size limit: send never waits.

slides.caption: Without backpressure memory can grow; prefer bounded channels for streams of work.
Handy for sending from sync code.

oneshot-channel.title: How tokio::sync::oneshot::channel works
oneshot-channel.description: A channel for exactly one value: send once, await once.

slides.caption: Typical use: send a request to a task together with a oneshot sender for the answer.
rx.await gets Ok(42), or Err if tx was dropped.
send() is not async: it never waits.

oneshot-send.title: How oneshot::Sender::send works
oneshot-send.description: Sends the one value; Err(value) if the receiver is gone.

slides.caption: Consumes the sender, so it can only be called once.
rx.await gives Err if tx is dropped unsent.

title.text: let (tx, mut rx1) = broadcast::channel(16); let mut rx2 = tx.subscribe();

slides.caption: Each receiver has its own position in a shared ring buffer. A slow receiver can lag and lose old messages.
subscribe() only sees messages sent after it.

broadcast-subscribe.title: How broadcast::Sender::subscribe works
broadcast-subscribe.description: Adds a new receiver that sees messages from now on.

slides.caption: receiver_count() tells how many there are.

watch-channel.title: How tokio::sync::watch::channel works
watch-channel.description: Holds one current value; receivers see the latest one and can wait for changes.

slides.caption: Only the newest value is kept. Receivers that were busy skip intermediate values.
tx.send("on") replaces it; readers now see "on".
changed().await waits for the next update.

watch-changed.title: How watch::Receiver::changed works
watch-changed.description: Waits until a new value is sent.

slides.caption: Err when the sender is dropped.
borrow_and_update marks the value as seen.

watch-send-modify.title: How watch::Sender::send_modify works
watch-send-modify.description: Changes the current value in place and notifies receivers.

slides.caption: Works even when no receiver exists.

mutex-lock.title: How tokio::sync::Mutex::lock works
mutex-lock.description: Waits for the lock asynchronously; the guard may be held across .await.

slides.caption: Use tokio's Mutex when the guard must live across an .await. For short critical sections std::sync::Mutex is faster.
Task 2 waits its turn, then adds 1.
No poisoning: a panic while locked does not poison it.

mutex-try-lock.title: How tokio::sync::Mutex::try_lock works
mutex-try-lock.description: Locks only if free right now.

rwlock-read.title: How tokio::sync::RwLock::read works
rwlock-read.description: A shared read lock: many readers at once.

slides.caption: Writers wait until all readers are done (and the lock is fair).
Waits for readers and other writers.

semaphore-acquire.title: How Semaphore::acquire works
semaphore-acquire.description: Waits for a permit; at most N holders at a time.

slides.caption: A semaphore with 2 permits lets 2 tasks in; the third waits until a permit is dropped.
None left: the next acquire waits.
Great for limiting parallel downloads or database connections.

semaphore-available-permits.title: How Semaphore::available_permits works
semaphore-available-permits.description: How many permits are free right now.

slides.caption: Dropping a permit gives it back.

semaphore-try-acquire.title: How Semaphore::try_acquire works
semaphore-try-acquire.description: Takes a permit only if one is free now.

notify-notify-one.title: How Notify::notify_one works
notify-notify-one.description: Wakes one task waiting on notified(); if none waits, the next one returns at once.

slides.caption: Only one stored permit: several notify_one calls before anyone waits count as one.

barrier-wait.title: How Barrier::wait works
barrier-wait.description: Waits until n tasks have reached the barrier, then releases them together.

slides.caption: Exactly one of them is told it is the leader.

oncecell-get-or-init.title: How tokio::sync::OnceCell::get_or_init works
oncecell-get-or-init.description: Initializes the value once with an async function; later calls reuse it.

slides.caption: Concurrent callers wait for the first initializer.

fs-read-to-string.title: How tokio::fs::read_to_string works
fs-read-to-string.description: Reads a whole file into a String, without blocking the runtime.

slides.caption: tokio::fs functions run the std::fs call on a blocking thread and await the result.
Err for missing files or invalid UTF-8.

fs-write.title: How tokio::fs::write works
fs-write.description: Writes bytes to a file, creating or replacing it.

fs-create-dir-all.title: How tokio::fs::create_dir_all works
fs-create-dir-all.description: Creates a folder and any missing parent folders.

slides.caption: No error if it already exists.
Create a, then b, then c.
create_dir creates only the last one.

fs-read-dir.title: How tokio::fs::read_dir works
fs-read-dir.description: Lists a folder: call next_entry() until it returns None.

slides.caption: Order is not guaranteed: sort if you need to.
Err if it does not exist.

fs-metadata.title: How tokio::fs::metadata works
fs-metadata.description: File size, type and times, asynchronously.

fs-copy.title: How tokio::fs::copy works
fs-copy.description: Copies a file; returns the number of bytes copied.

fs-try-exists.title: How tokio::fs::try_exists works
fs-try-exists.description: Ok(true) or Ok(false) for whether a path exists; Err if it cannot tell.

slides.caption: Unlike Path::exists, permission errors are reported.
Avoid check-then-open races where you can.

read-to-string.title: How AsyncReadExt::read_to_string works
read-to-string.description: Reads everything from an async reader into a String.

slides.caption: Returns the number of bytes read.

read-exact.title: How AsyncReadExt::read_exact works
read-exact.description: Fills the whole buffer, or fails with UnexpectedEof.

slides.caption: Good for headers of known length.

read-u32.title: How AsyncReadExt::read_u32 works
read-u32.description: Reads 4 bytes as a big-endian u32.

slides.caption: There are versions for every integer size.

write-all.title: How AsyncWriteExt::write_all works
write-all.description: Writes the whole buffer, looping until every byte is written.

slides.caption: write() may write only part; write_all keeps going.
Call flush() if the writer buffers.

flush.title: How AsyncWriteExt::flush works
flush.description: Pushes buffered bytes out to the underlying writer.

slides.caption: Without it, BufWriter keeps data until it is full or dropped.

lines.title: How AsyncBufReadExt::lines works
lines.description: Turns a buffered reader into a stream of lines.

slides.caption: Wrap a file or socket in BufReader first. next_line() returns Ok(None) at the end.

read-line.title: How AsyncBufReadExt::read_line works
read-line.description: Reads one line, including its \n, appending it to a String.

slides.caption: Read up to the line break.
lines() strips the line break for you.

runtime-new.title: How Runtime::new works
runtime-new.description: Creates a multi-threaded runtime, to run async code from sync code.

runtime-block-on.title: How Runtime::block_on works
runtime-block-on.description: Runs a future to completion, blocking the current thread.

slides.caption: Do not call it from inside async code: that panics.
Handle::block_on works with an existing runtime handle.

builder-new-current-thread.title: How Builder::new_current_thread works
builder-new-current-thread.description: Configures a runtime that runs everything on the current thread.

slides.caption: enable_all() turns on timers and I/O.

builder-worker-threads.title: How Builder::worker_threads works
builder-worker-threads.description: Sets how many worker threads a multi-thread runtime uses.

slides.caption: The default is one per CPU core.
Blocking work uses a separate pool.

handle-current.title: How Handle::current works
handle-current.description: A handle to the runtime the current code runs on.

slides.caption: Panics outside a runtime; try_current returns a Result.
Pass the handle to threads that need to spawn tasks.

tcp-listener-bind.title: How tokio::net::TcpListener::bind works
tcp-listener-bind.description: Opens a TCP socket listening on an address.

slides.caption: bind is async in tokio. The listener then accepts connections with accept().await.
Create the socket and bind the address.
Port 0 lets the OS choose a free port.
Use "0.0.0.0:8080" to accept connections from other machines.

tcp-listener-accept.title: How tokio::net::TcpListener::accept works
tcp-listener-accept.description: Waits for the next incoming connection.

slides.caption: Spawn a task per connection to serve many at once.

tcp-stream-connect.title: How tokio::net::TcpStream::connect works
tcp-stream-connect.description: Opens a TCP connection to an address.

slides.caption: Read and write with AsyncReadExt / AsyncWriteExt.

tcp-listener-local-addr.title: How tokio::net::TcpListener::local_addr works
tcp-listener-local-addr.description: The address the listener is bound to (with the real port).

slides.caption: peer_addr() on a stream gives the other side.

io-copy.title: How tokio::io::copy works
io-copy.description: Copies everything from a reader to a writer; returns the byte count.

io-duplex.title: How tokio::io::duplex works
io-duplex.description: An in-memory pipe with two connected ends, like a fake socket.

slides.caption: What one end writes, the other reads.
Great for tests without real sockets.

instant-elapsed.title: How tokio::time::Instant::elapsed works
instant-elapsed.description: Time passed since the instant, using tokio's clock.

slides.caption: Follows tokio's paused clock in tests (start_paused).
